first_reaction_normalization.selected_equation: 2 KEGG:C00138 + CHEBI:57288 + CHEBI:16526 + CHEBI:15378 -> 2 KEGG:C00139 + CHEBI:15361 + CHEBI:57287
first_reaction_normalization.derivation: Both neutral CoA forms lose four H, so their shifts cancel. Product pyruvic acid loses one H; cancel that released product H against two native input H to obtain one input H. Generic carrier protonation/redox labels are retained, with no specific protein/cluster assignment.
first_reaction_normalization.reason: Generic KEGG ferredoxins lack formula/charge; only explicit acid-base bookkeeping is checked. No measured proton or exact carrier-cluster stoichiometry claim.

rows.assertion: Pyruvate-acceptor oxidoreductase was measured with methyl viologen; pyruvate-carboxyl 14CO2 exchange was also measured. These assays do not identify the physiological ferredoxin or select among the candidate locus groups.
Extract pyruvate-water dikinase formed PEP with ATP; a discontinuous PEP assay was used. This is the AMP/phosphate-forming reaction, not an inferred pyruvate-kinase reversal.
PEP carboxylase activity was measured by coupled NADH oxidation and radiochemical bicarbonate incorporation. MnCl2 was an assay component, not a demonstrated native metal-occupancy result.
Extract malate dehydrogenase was measured by oxaloacetate-dependent NADH oxidation. This record preserves that NADH-dependent chemistry.
Extract fumarate hydratase was assayed anaerobically with D,L-malate. The selected stereospecific physiological malate reaction is separately grounded in Rhea.
Extract fumarate reductase used reduced methyl viologen. This assay does not establish quinol or a specific ferredoxin as its physiological electron donor.
Extract succinyl-CoA synthetase used succinate, ATP and CoA, coupled to recombinant M. sedula reductase. NADPH belonged to the coupling reaction, not the synthetase stoichiometry.
Extract succinyl-CoA reductase was measured with succinyl-CoA and NADPH. The T. neutrophilus reaction is distinguished from the donor-unspecified I. hospitalis activity.
Extract succinic semialdehyde reductase was measured with succinic semialdehyde and NADPH.
4-Hydroxybutyrate-CoA ligase was measured with 4-hydroxybutyrate, ATP and CoA by discontinuous CoA consumption.
Extract 4-hydroxybutyryl-CoA dehydratase was assayed by detecting crotonyl-CoA with an added R. sphaeroides coupling enzyme; coupling-enzyme cofactors are not transferred.
Crotonyl-CoA hydratase was assayed in reverse with (R)- or (S)-3-hydroxybutyryl-CoA. Activity occurred only with the (S) substrate.
Extract (S)-3-hydroxybutyryl-CoA dehydrogenase reduced NAD+. No activity was detected with NADP+ or the (R) substrate.
Thiolase activity was measured by HPLC detection of acetyl-CoA from acetoacetyl-CoA and CoA.
Tneu_1204 is a candidate pyruvate-water dikinase in Table 1; the measured activity is from extract, not purified Tneu_1204.
Tneu_0418 is the Table 1 candidate PEP carboxylase; activity is demonstrated in extract, not purified Tneu_0418.
Tneu_1509 is the Table 1 candidate malate dehydrogenase; the NADH-dependent reaction is demonstrated in extract.
Table 1 assigns Tneu_1334/1335 as putative fumarate-hydratase subunits. The direct activity is in extract; individual subunit sufficiency and exact assembly stoichiometry were not measured.
Table 1 assigns Tneu_1334/1335 as putative fumarate-hydratase subunits. The direct activity is in extract; individual subunit sufficiency and exact assembly stoichiometry were not measured.
Issue377 exact source span for separately qualified locus/purified-species attribution.

T. neutrophilus fumarate reductase was soluble and active with reduced viologens but not NAD(P)H. Tneu_0423/0424 are putative induced subunits. Generic A/AH2 retains the unresolved physiological donor instead of native module quinol chemistry.

Tneu_0423/0424 are putative fumarate-reductase subunits induced during autotrophic growth. Soluble extract activity uses reduced viologens, not NAD(P)H; neither isolated subunit is asserted to catalyze the whole reaction.

Tneu_0423/0424 are putative fumarate-reductase subunits induced during autotrophic growth. Soluble extract activity uses reduced viologens, not NAD(P)H; neither isolated subunit is asserted to catalyze the whole reaction.
Tneu_1463 and Tneu_1464 are the two autotrophy-induced succinyl-CoA synthetase subunits. Their joint role does not establish that each independently catalyzes the reaction.
Tneu_1463 and Tneu_1464 are the two autotrophy-induced succinyl-CoA synthetase subunits. Their joint role does not establish that each independently catalyzes the reaction.

Tneu_0421 was expressed in E. coli as soluble N-terminal His10-tagged protein and purified. It reduced succinyl-CoA with NADPH, with 10% activity using NADH; malonyl-CoA and methylmalonyl-CoA were inactive.
Tneu_0419 was expressed in E. coli as soluble N-terminal His10-tagged protein and purified. It catalyzed NADPH-dependent reduction of succinic semialdehyde.

Purified recombinant Tneu_0420 acted on 4-hydroxybutyrate. Lys594 acetylation was detected in the E. coli-produced protein and may be an expression artifact; native archaeal regulatory acetylation is not established.
Tneu_0422 is assigned by sequence similarity alongside extract dehydratase activity. Purified T. neutrophilus enzyme, assembly and Fe-S/FAD occupancy were not demonstrated in this study.
Tneu_0541 is a candidate hydratase/dehydrogenase fusion identified by domain similarity. The purified native and recombinant enzyme tested in this section is Msed_0399, not Tneu_0541.
The authors infer that the fusion protein operates in anaerobic crenarchaeal carbon fixation because it is the only candidate for these two activities; this is not a purified Tneu_0541 experiment.
Tneu_0249 was expressed as soluble N-terminal His10-tagged protein in E. coli. The purified enzyme cleaved acetoacetyl-CoA thiolytically into two acetyl-CoA molecules.
Issue377 exact source span for separately qualified locus/purified-species attribution.
